Hi Alex & Sam -

Thanks again for a productive call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the customer-led load test scheduled:

Summary of targets we heard from your side
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 350ms, p99 <= 800ms (for request/response paths)
- Throughput target: ~200 req/s sustained for peak windows
- Concurrent users: expected peak concurrency ~50-75 concurrent requests
- Streaming: required for the chat flows (chunked SSE; client expects partial tokens within 200-300ms of generation)

What Redwood will provide
- Test accounts/API keys + a sandbox model endpoint (sandbox.redwood-inference.com)
- A baseline k6 script (finwise_k6_script_v1.js) and a Locust file (finwise_locustfile_v1.py) you can adapt
- IP ranges to allowlist for the test window
- SRE monitoring during the test and a shared post-test report

Proposed test window (please confirm):
- Thu, Jun 18 - 09:00-11:00 PT (02:00-04:00 UTC) - short warm-up then 90 mins at target load

Immediate asks for your team
1) Confirm test window or propose an alternate 2-hour block
2) Confirm whether you'll run k6 or Locust and who will own the runner
3) Confirm any additional success criteria beyond the SLOs above (e.g., error rate < 1%)

Attached: finwise_k6_script_v1.js (starter), test-account-readme.md

Thanks - I'll loop Neha (CSM) in once we have a confirmed slot so she can coordinate the post-test debrief.

--Marissa

Hey team - a few technical notes from SRE side to make the test actionable and safe: 

Recommended ramp schedule
- 10m gentle warm-up at 10-20% of target
- 20m linear ramp to 100%
- 60m steady state at target load
- 10m cool-down

Warm-up is important: we have prefix/KV caches and JIT paths that need a short run to stabilize p95/p99. If you jump immediately to 100% you'll measure cold penalties.

Observability & metrics we'll capture (we'll share a Grafana snapshot):
- p50/p95/p99 latency (request and token-level where applicable)
- error rates (4xx/5xx) and 429s
- model pod CPU/GPU utilization and queue lengths

On streaming: if you use SSE, please ensure your k6/Locust runner treats streaming responses as long-lived connections - otherwise the runner may timeout. We recommend a 10s response timeout for chunked streams.

I'll be online the entire window and will post live notes to the shared Drive doc. If anything looks off we'll throttle and communicate.

--Rishi
